rows.name: CABAL_INSTALL
rows.who_sets: `flake.nix` in the Nix dev shell, and the CI workflows.
rows.read_by: `make` in `ingest`, `cmake`, the ingest Python tools and CI scripts (`ingest/Makefile`, `ingest/CMakeLists.txt`, `ingest/build-model.py` and 7 more files)
rows.values: Name or path of the `cabal` program (the Haskell build tool). Only CMake checks that the program exists. `make CABAL_INSTALL=value` also works in `ingest/Makefile`.
rows.default: Unset: `ingest/Makefile`, the Python tools and `bin/ci/install-sydtest-discover.sh` run `cabal`. Empty: only the Python tools differ. They use the empty text as the command.
rows.effect: Selects the `cabal` program for the ingest Haskell code. `ingest/Makefile` runs it for the targets `test` and `test-coverage`. `ingest/build-model.py` and `ingest/runtime/tron_ingest_tools/ingest.py` run ingest through it only when the caller gives no ingest executable.
rows.notes: CMake (`ingest/CMakeLists.txt`) searches the name `cabal` before the value. It uses the value only when that search finds nothing. When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not set, CMake searches `cabal-3.16.0.0` first, and configure stops unless the found program reports version 3.16.0.0.

rows.values: Any text. `GNUmakefile` only prints it. `make CMAKE_DEFINES=value` also works.

rows.name: COMPILER_RT_BUILTINS_ROOT
rows.who_sets: `flake.nix`, for the Nix dev shell and the Nix CMake builds.
rows.values: Directory path. CMake searches it for the library `clang_rt.builtins-x86_64`. The Nix files set `${llvm19.compiler-rt}/lib/linux`.
rows.effect: CMake searches this directory for the compiler-rt builtins library (an LLVM runtime library) before `/usr/lib/llvm-19/lib/clang/19/lib/linux`. CMake links the library that it finds into libtron. Configure stops with the error `clang_rt.builtins-x86_64 library not found` when neither directory holds the library.
rows.notes: `find_library` uses `NO_DEFAULT_PATH`. CMake searches no other directory. CMake keeps the result in the cache variable `COMPILER_RT_BUILTINS`. A build tree that already holds a result does not search again.

rows.name: DEBUG
rows.values: `GNUmakefile`: any non-empty text counts as set, `0` included. `bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile`: `0` selects the optimised build, and any other text selects the debug build. `make DEBUG=1` also works.
rows.default: Unset: `GNUmakefile` prints no extra lines. `bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile` uses `1`, the debug build with `-O0 -ggdb`.
rows.effect: `GNUmakefile` prints the values of `BUILD_TYPE`, `MAKEFLAGS`, `TESTS`, `PHONY`, `RUN` and `CMAKE_DEFINES` while it parses, and changes nothing else. In `bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile` (the makefile of iotools, a third-party I/O tool copied into the repository), `0` compiles with `-O2 -DNDEBUG`.
rows.notes: The two makefiles use the same name for different purposes. A `DEBUG` that is exported for another tool also turns on the `GNUmakefile` output. No TRON build file runs the iotools makefile.

rows.name: ENABLE_FUSE_STATS
rows.who_sets: Developers who build without FUSE stats.
rows.values: Text for the CMake option `ENABLE_FUSE_STATS`, for example `ON` or `OFF`. The makefile passes the text without a check. `make ENABLE_FUSE_STATS=OFF` also works.
rows.default: Unset: `ON`. Empty: the makefile passes the empty text to CMake, and CMake counts empty text as off.
rows.effect: Selects at CMake configure time whether FUSE stats are compiled into the programs. `GNUmakefile` passes the text to `cmake` as `-DENABLE_FUSE_STATS=<value>`. A changed value rewrites the file `gen/.fuse_stats_stamp`, and `make` then runs CMake configure again.
rows.notes: `GNUmakefile` passes the value only for builds in `gen/` and for `make deb`. The sanitizer, coverage and `deb-host` builds do not get it. For a build on an LSF worker (`REMOTE`), a `make` command-line value and a non-empty environment value reach the worker.

evidence.quote: for var in ENABLE_FUSE_STATS CCACHE_DISABLE XDG_CACHE_HOME; do

rows.name: FUSE_STATS_STAMP
rows.values: File path. This is an internal make variable. `GNUmakefile` assigns it and ignores an environment value, except when the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`.
rows.default: Unset: `gen/.fuse_stats_stamp`. When the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`, the text is empty.
rows.effect: An environment value changes no build result. For the goals `list-tests` and `list-tests-core` alone, `make` puts the value into the prerequisite lists of the CMake configure targets and the package target. `make` does not build those targets for these goals.
rows.notes: The file holds the last `ENABLE_FUSE_STATS` value. A changed file makes `make` run CMake configure again. `make FUSE_STATS_STAMP=path` on the command line replaces the path for every goal.

rows.name: HAS_AVX512
rows.values: Only the text `no` has an effect. On Linux the makefile assigns `yes` or `no` itself and ignores an environment value. On macOS it uses the environment value.
rows.default: Unset: on Linux, `yes` when `/proc/cpuinfo` lists the flag `avx512f`, otherwise `no`. On macOS, empty text.
rows.effect: `no` means that the CPU of the build host lacks AVX-512 (a CPU instruction set). `make t_<name>` then builds the test and stops with an error before the run. When `REMOTE` is `0`, `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga`, `test-fast` and `test-proxy` stop with an error and build nothing.
rows.notes: `make HAS_AVX512=value` on the command line replaces the detected value on Linux too. The `-old` test targets stop in the same way. The sanitizer and coverage targets do not check the variable.

evidence.quote: @echo "Error: Cannot run $@: cross-compiled for AVX-512. Run tests on a machine with AVX-512." >&2; exit 1

rows.name: NPROC_BUILD
rows.who_sets: CI workflows, the Nix build and `bin/bsub-build`.
rows.read_by: `make`, the Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build`, CI workflows (`GNUmakefile`, `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh`, `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` and 2 more files)
rows.values: Positive integer, a number of parallel jobs. `GNUmakefile` passes the text to `-j` without a check. `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh` accepts only digits with no leading `0`. `make NPROC_BUILD=4` also works.
rows.default: Unset: `GNUmakefile` uses the smaller of 16 jobs and the `nproc` output. `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh` stops with the error `NPROC_BUILD is required`.

rows.name: PRESET_STAMP
rows.values: File path. This is an internal make variable. `GNUmakefile` assigns it and ignores an environment value, except when the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`.

rows.name: REMOTE
rows.who_sets: Developers. `bin/bsub-build` sets `0` inside the LSF job.
rows.values: Exactly one of `0`, `1`, `sku0`, `sku1`. Spaces around the value are removed. Any other text stops `make` with an error. `make REMOTE=1` also works.
rows.default: Unset: the value of `TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION` (default `0`) for build goals and test goals, and `0` for other goals. Empty: `make` stops with an error.
rows.effect: `0` runs everything on the local host. `1`, `sku0` and `sku1` send the goals `all`, `build`, `core`, `build-core`, `build-prod`, `build-test`, `build-ingest`, `build-test-host` and `build-test-fpga` to an LSF worker through `bin/bsub-build`. They also add `--remote` to `bin/slice run` for `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga` and `test-fast`.
rows.notes: `sku0` and `sku1` also add `--remote-sku=<value>` (a server class of the test pool). With `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`, `make` stops with an error for goals that run tests directly, for example `run`, `t_<name>`, `test-proxy` and the coverage goals. Other goals run on the local host.

evidence.quote: $(error $(REMOTE_MODE_SOURCE) must be one of 0, 1, sku0, or sku1)
all build core build-core build-prod build-test build-ingest build-test-host build-test-fpga:

rows.name: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES
rows.values: Positive integer, a number of cores. Text with a character other than a digit, or the text `0`, stops the script with exit code 2.
rows.effect: Sets the number of cores that the LSF build job reserves. The script exports the same number on the worker as `NPROC_BUILD` and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`. It also sets the default of `REMOTE_BUILD_MEM`, 8192 MB for each core.
rows.notes: A `-jN` flag of `make` replaces this variable with N. A comment in `GNUmakefile` says that GNU make 4.3 sees `-jN` only when N differs from `NPROC_BUILD`. A value with a leading `0` passes the check, and the memory default reads it in base 8.

evidence.quote: echo "bsub-build: $2 must be a positive integer, got '$1'" >&2

rows.name: REMOTE_BUILD_MEM
rows.who_sets: Developers, before a build on an LSF worker.
rows.values: A number of MB (megabytes). The script does not check the text. It passes the text to `bsub` in `rusage[mem=<value>]`.
rows.default: Unset: 8192 MB for each core of `REMOTE_BUILD_CORES`. That is 131072 MB for the default of 16 cores.
rows.effect: Sets the memory that the LSF build job reserves.
rows.notes: The script comment says `8 GB per core` for the default, and the log line adds the suffix `M`. The repository holds no LSF configuration that confirms the unit of `rusage[mem=]`. `make` runs `bin/bsub-build` only when `REMOTE` is `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`.

evidence.quote: # 8 GB per core. The generated models_*.cpp units cost 5-6 GB in a single

rows.name: REMOTE_BUILD_QUEUE
rows.who_sets: Developers, before a build on an LSF worker.
rows.values: Name of an LSF queue. The script passes the text to `bsub -q` without a check.
rows.effect: Selects the LSF queue that receives the build job.

new_terms.definition: The script that submits a build command to an LSF worker and streams the output back. `make` runs it for build goals when `REMOTE` is `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`.
Two server classes of the remote test pool. `REMOTE=sku0` or `REMOTE=sku1` selects one for the test run. A build treats both as `1`.
The Haskell build tool that builds, runs and tests ingest.
The Python package tool that creates the Python environments outside the Nix dev shell.
A CPU instruction set. Every TRON build compiles for it, also on a host whose CPU does not have it.
A third-party I/O tool. A copy is in `bin/iotools-1.5`. No TRON build file builds it.
include-what-you-use, the tool that checks the include lines of C++ files.
The Nix derivation `tron-cmake-test-build`, the check `cmake-sandbox-configure` and the dev shell `cmake-sandbox`. All three take their environment from `cmakeSandboxEnvironment` in `flake.nix`.
The LLVM runtime library `clang_rt.builtins-x86_64`. CMake links it into libtron.
The directory `/nix/store`. It holds the packages that Nix builds.
A named set of CMake settings in `CMakePresets.json`. `GNUmakefile` uses `native` on Linux and `darwin` on macOS for the `gen/` build.

notes: All 18 rows are kept. No row is dropped. Rows changed in meaning: CABAL_INSTALL, ENABLE_FUSE_STATS, HAS_AVX512, INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION, NPROC_BUILD, REMOTE, REMOTE_BUILD_MEM. The other changes are wording, format or evidence. Open decision: FUSE_STATS_STAMP, PRESET_STAMP and HAS_AVX512 are internal make variables. They stay with drop false. The environment reaches make on one path each (the goals list-tests and list-tests-core alone, or macOS), and a make command-line value replaces all three. Open decision: DEBUG has two readers with different meaning in one row, as the format allows one row for each name. Seven evidence quotes are an exact part of the source line and not the whole line: GNUmakefile:96, :245, :358, :362 and :578 (the whole line holds a vertical bar character), and GNUmakefile:399 and :682 (the whole line has more than 120 characters). Checks on stand-alone copies outside the checkout (GNU Make 4.3, CMake 3.22.1, bash 5.1.16), with nothing of the repository built or run: an empty environment value counts as unset for ifndef and ifdef and is kept by ?=. A command-line value replaces a := assignment. An empty REMOTE has origin environment and zero words. A -jN equal to NPROC_BUILD is not seen in the recipe under make 4.3. find_program uses an ENV value in NAMES only after the listed names. -DENABLE_FUSE_STATS= with no value makes if(ENABLE_FUSE_STATS) false. bash reads 010 as octal 8 and stops on 08. Not settled from the checkout: the unit that the LSF cluster applies to rusage[mem=].

They also add `--remote` to `bin/slice run` for `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga` and `test-fast`.

changes.name: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES
changes.was: When `REMOTE` sends the build to an LSF worker, `make -jN` overrides this variable with N. With GNU make 4.3, the makefile detects `-jN` only when N differs from `NPROC_BUILD`. A leading `0` passes the check, and the memory default reads the value as octal.
changes.now: A `-jN` flag of `make` replaces this variable with N. A comment in `GNUmakefile` says that GNU make 4.3 sees `-jN` only when N differs from `NPROC_BUILD`. A value with a leading `0` passes the check, and the memory default reads it in base 8.
changes.why: Wording. The statement about GNU make 4.3 now names its source, the comment at GNUmakefile:202 to :205. A stand-alone copy of GNUmakefile:206 to :209 under GNU make 4.3 gave the same result. bash 5.1.16 computed 65536 for `010`, and stopped with an error for `08` (bin/bsub-build:21, :32).
